sources.entry: Candela - Protects your displays from OLED burn-in and wear: panel health history, a checkup for defects, and the everyday brightness, volume, and scaling controls macOS leaves out.

summary.one_liner: Candela is a free, open-source macOS menu-bar app that protects OLED and other displays from burn-in and wear, with panel health records, a diagnostic checkup, and monitor controls macOS lacks.
summary.what_it_does: Candela watches on-screen content and eases down bright regions that stay unchanged to reduce burn-in, while live content stays at full brightness. It keeps a coarse-grid health map of where an enrolled panel has been lit, plus panel hours and per-app time, and exports the record as an integrity-checked file. A guided checkup looks for defects and wear on any display and grades each result as observed, refused, not observed, or self-reported. Controls cover DDC/CI brightness, contrast and volume for external monitors, software dimming below the hardware floor, an HDR toggle, HiDPI resolutions macOS hides, arrangement, mirroring, rotation and virtual displays. It also offers menu-bar and Dock auto-hide and dims the screen when you step away or lock the Mac.
use_cases: protect an OLED monitor from burn-in
track panel hours and display wear over time
diagnose defects on a used or new monitor
adjust external monitor brightness and volume from the Mac
enable HiDPI or custom scaled resolutions on macOS
auto-hide the menu bar and Dock
how_to_run: Download the notarized build from the latest release or candela.fyi, open the disk image, and drag Candela to Applications.
Or install with Homebrew: brew install --cask rydersel/tap/candela
notable: Adaptive real-time burn-in defense that dims unchanged bright regions while leaving live content untouched
Health map and panel-hours record stored as a coarse grid, so screen content is not kept
Guided checkup that grades every finding as observed, refused, not observed, or self-reported
DDC/CI control of external monitor brightness, contrast and volume, including write-only panels tracked by last value sent
Signed auto-updates; mismatched signatures are refused
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon
Some features (mode switching, virtual displays, HDR toggle, menu-bar auto-hide) rely on undocumented private macOS APIs that may break with new macOS releases
Hardware brightness, contrast and volume depend on the monitor supporting DDC/CI over the connected cable
